result.rationale: The diff shows in GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet the `find` compares against that same falsy value, so it can never match and always yields undefined — the old working fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. The same broken pattern appears in updateEvent at line 253. This is a genuine dead-condition regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which cannot select the intended destination calendar, yielding `undefined` and forcing downstream fallback behavior (e.g., `"primary"` in createEvent and likely similar in update/delete). This makes updates/deletes fail or target the wrong calendar when the booking relied on `destinationCalendar` rather than an explicit `externalCalendarId`.
